clue.text: Something worth having in the form prescribed

parts.note: as can mean in the form or role of, as in dressed as a pirate
set means laid down or prescribed, as in a set text

explanation.surface: A doctor's prescription, taken exactly as directed, turns out to be worth having.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one phrase about following a doctor's orders; the definition comes first and the two short words follow.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is a valuable possession or useful quality, something one is glad to own.

clue.text: Soldier who drops in appropriate American equipment

indicators.note: in puts the soldier inside the word for appropriate

parts.note: apt means appropriate or fitting
a para is a paratrooper, a soldier who drops by parachute

explanation.surface: A paratrooper drops in to seize some American kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drops in' sounds like a casual visit; the soldier drops by parachute and goes in the word APT.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparatus is the gear or equipment needed for a task.

clue.text: Addition to letter upset cashiers

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the word is turned upside down, read from bottom to top

parts.note: to cashier is to dismiss, so cashiers means fires

explanation.surface: A postscript added to a letter has distressed the bank tellers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cashiers' looks like bank staff, but is the verb to dismiss; 'upset' turns FIRES round.
explanation.definitionFit: A serif is the small stroke added at the end of a printed letter's main lines.

clue.text: Such holiday offers in newspaper go fast

parts.note: The Times, the newspaper this puzzle appears in
to hare is to run very fast

explanation.surface: Bargain holiday deals advertised in the paper are quickly snapped up.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a sales pitch; the paper is The Times itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Timeshare means part-ownership of a holiday flat by the week, sold as packages to buyers.

clue.text: Way in which police force evolved

definitions.text: Way in which police force evolved

parts.words: Way in which police force evolved
parts.note: read 'Way' as a street rather than a method: the London street where the Runners, forerunners of the Metropolitan Police, were based

explanation.surface: A history lesson on the manner in which policing developed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Way' looks like 'method' but means a road. The Bow Street Runners, set up in the 1740s at the magistrates' court in this London street, were Britain's first organised police force.
explanation.definitionFit: The London thoroughfare housing the magistrates' court that founded the Runners, an early professional constabulary.

clue.text: Possess .a piece of furniture? Wrong

parts.note: a bed is a piece of bedroom furniture
wrong as a noun means evil, wickedness

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about whether owning a piece of furniture could be sinful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possess' looks like 'own', but means take hold of like a demon.
explanation.definitionFit: To be possessed is to be tormented by a spirit, which is what bedevilling someone does.

clue.text: Darkness imminent here in Ireland?

parts.note: a candle's burnt-down wick means dark is coming; the two words for that make the name of an Irish county

explanation.surface: Night is about to fall in some place in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: A candle with its wick low is about to go out; County Wicklow lies south of Dublin.
explanation.definitionFit: An Irish county south of Dublin, whose name splits into words for a burnt-down candle thread.

clue.text: Attempt bribery, say, in American city

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: to tamper with a witness or jury is to try to bribe or interfere

explanation.surface: Someone tries to bribe officials in a US city.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech the final R of TAMPER is silent, so it matches TAMPA.
explanation.definitionFit: Tampa is a city on the Gulf coast of Florida.

clue.text: Sociable actor, temporarily lacking a public

indicators.note: lacking says the word that follows is missing from the actor

parts.note: an extra is a film actor taken on temporarily for a crowd scene
overt means public, done openly

explanation.surface: An outgoing actor finds himself without an audience for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking a public' looks like 'without an audience', but 'lacking' takes only the A away from the temporary actor; 'public' then stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: An extrovert is outgoing and gregarious, a person who enjoys company.

clue.text: The sort of floor covering on which debauchery occurs

definitions.text: The sort of floor covering on which debauchery occurs

parts.words: The sort of floor covering on which debauchery occurs
parts.note: a night 'on the' squares of fired clay is a riotous night out, in the British phrase

explanation.surface: Wild behaviour takes place on a particular sort of flooring.
explanation.walkthrough: To be 'on the tiles' is a British idiom for a night of wild revelry, originally of cats on rooftops.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceramic squares cover floors and roofs, and the idiom places carousing on top of them.

clue.text: Doctor's assistant giving quiet care amid disorder

parts.note: P (piano) is the musical abbreviation for quiet

indicators.note: the letters of the preceding words are thrown into disorder and rearranged

explanation.surface: A hospital helper provides calm nursing in the middle of chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disorder' looks like part of the scene, but it rearranges P, CARE and AMID.
explanation.definitionFit: A paramedic is trained medical staff who supports doctors, typically on ambulance crews.

clue.text: For example, lead given by spy chief and others

parts.note: M is the head of the secret service in the James Bond stories
et al is the Latin abbreviation for 'and others'

explanation.surface: A tip-off is handed over by the spymaster and his colleagues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' reads as a clue or tip in a spy story, but it is the heavy element.
explanation.definitionFit: Lead is one example of a metal, alongside iron, tin and copper.

clue.text: Pope's collars

definitions.meaning: read as the plural 'popes': the pope is a small freshwater fish of the perch family, also called the ruffe
frilled starched neckwear of Elizabethan fashion

explanation.surface: The neckwear worn by the head of the Catholic Church.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests papal vestments, but the pope here is a fish, also known by the answer's name (often spelt with a final E).
explanation.definitionFit: The fish called the pope is also named ruff or ruffe, and Elizabethan pleated neck frills bear the same name.

clue.text: Reform can solve nothing as result of earthly divisions

indicators.note: reform tells us to re-form, that is rebuild, the letters of the words that follow

parts.note: O, the round zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A political claim that reform settles nothing, given how divided the world is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'earthly divisions' sounds like world politics, but it means the boundaries between the earth's crustal plates.
explanation.definitionFit: Eruptive mountains mostly form where tectonic plates meet or pull apart, so they arise from splits in the earth's crust.

clue.text: Pat's oil, perhaps, the first canvas we view?

indicators.note: perhaps suggests these letters might be arranged some other way

parts.note: the S of the possessive is needed as a letter here

explanation.surface: An art lover wonders whether Pat's oil painting is the first picture on show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canvas' and 'oil' suggest painting, but canvas means sailcloth: the highest sail is the first part of a ship seen over the horizon.
explanation.definitionFit: A topsail sits above the lower sails, so its sailcloth is what an observer spots first as a ship approaches.

clue.text: He may have to concoct court plea

definitions.text: He may have to concoct court plea

indicators.note: to concoct is to cook up, so the two words are cooked into a new order

explanation.surface: An accused man may need to make up a story for the judge.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: an embezzler on trial may have to invent a plea, and 'concoct' rearranges COURT PLEA.
explanation.definitionFit: A peculator embezzles funds, and such a fraudster in the dock may need an invented defence.

clue.text: Partners back this movie

parts.note: we is how two partners refer to themselves together
the stern is the back of a ship

explanation.surface: A couple of investors put their money behind a particular film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like a verb meaning finance, but it gives the rear of a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A western is a film genre of cowboys and the American frontier.

clue.text: Martyr — isn't small change needed in his original name?

indicators.note: in puts the slang and the coin inside the saint's earlier name

parts.note: Saul was the name of the apostle before his conversion
ain't is the colloquial form of isn't
P, a penny, is small change

explanation.surface: A question whether the martyr's original name needs a small alteration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small change' sounds like a slight alteration, but is a penny coin; the apostle was renamed after his conversion on the road to Damascus.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostle was executed in Rome for his faith, so he is counted among Christian martyrs.

clue.text: Wind a chap up on the railway

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Ron is a man's name, any chap

explanation.surface: Someone cranks up a man on the train line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' looks like the verb (rhyming with 'find') but is the noun; RON turned up gives NOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A wind from the north is called by that direction, as a southerly comes from the south.

clue.text: Take top place, or come next

definitions.meaning: to achieve success, to win through
to follow on, as an heir takes over a throne

explanation.surface: Advice to a competitor: either win, or settle for second.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both triumphing and following someone in a post, as a monarch's heir does.

clue.text: In new dance, attempt this figure

indicators.note: In puts the attempt inside the rearranged dance
new means the letters of dance are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: a go is an attempt

explanation.surface: Someone tries out a figure in a new dance routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'figure' sounds like a dance figure, but is a geometric shape; 'new' rearranges the dance as DECAN before the attempt goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: A decagon is a plane shape with ten sides.

clue.text: Dog Star

definitions.meaning: a breed of gundog that stands rigid to show where game lies
the two stars of the Plough that line up with the Pole Star

explanation.surface: The Dog Star, Sirius, the brightest in the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: The two words read together as Sirius, but each is a separate definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A hunting breed named for indicating game, and either of the two stars in Ursa Major used to locate Polaris.

clue.text: Champion in China, a big noise

parts.note: china plate is Cockney rhyming slang for mate, so china means pal
a din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: A celebrity champion in China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country but is rhyming slang: in Cockney, china plate means mate.
explanation.definitionFit: A paladin was one of Charlemagne's knights, so a heroic defender of a cause.

clue.text: Contentious claim fabricated by staff

parts.note: a staff is a long pole

indicators.note: fabricated means made up, so the word claim is made up into a new order

explanation.surface: Staff members are accused of making up a disputed allegation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' suggests employees, but it is a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: Polemical writing is argumentative and aggressive, provoking dispute.

clue.text: Roly-poly or fruit pie that is removed

parts.note: a plum is a fruit

indicators.note: removed says the abbreviation for that is comes out of pie

parts.note: ie is short for id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: Choosing between a jam roly-poly and a fruit pie, with one taken away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roly-poly' looks like the pudding, but is the adjective for chubby. Taking IE from PIE leaves P.
explanation.definitionFit: Plump and roly-poly both describe someone round and chubby.

clue.text: Married cunning little women, so-called

parts.note: arch means sly or knowing

explanation.surface: Wed women who are sly and small, as people describe them.
explanation.walkthrough: Little Women is Louisa May Alcott's novel about the four sisters of the family of that name: Meg, Jo, Beth and Amy.
explanation.definitionFit: The heroines of Alcott's novel share this surname, so they are the girls of that family.

clue.text: What masters do with a head after start of term

indicators.note: after places the second piece behind the first in the answer
start of takes just the opening letter of the word term

parts.note: each means per head, as in five pounds each

explanation.surface: A school scene: what the masters get up to with the headmaster once term begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'masters' and 'head' suggest a school staffroom, but 'a head' means per person.
explanation.definitionFit: Schoolmasters instruct pupils; that is their job.

clue.text: Herbert initially is a little pest

parts.note: A. P. Herbert, the humorist and MP, had the initials APH

explanation.surface: Someone called Herbert seems at first to be a minor nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' looks like 'take the first letter', but means the man's initials: A P Herbert signed as APH.
explanation.definitionFit: An aphis is a greenfly or other aphid, a tiny insect that damages garden plants.

clue.text: Sort of barrister without any qualifications

definitions.meaning: an ... barrister is a junior counsel, one who pleads outside the bar rather than a QC

explanation.surface: A lawyer who has passed no exams at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'qualifications' looks like exam certificates, but means reservations or limits.
explanation.definitionFit: In English law an utter barrister is one below Queen's Counsel; as an adjective the word means total or unmitigated.

clue.text: Sponsor a criminal leader

definitions.meaning: one who stands sponsor for a child at baptism
the head of a Mafia family

explanation.surface: Someone funds a crime boss.
explanation.definitionFit: A baptismal sponsor promises to oversee a child's faith, and the title also names a Mafia boss, as in the famous film.

clue.text: Standard appears at that point on temple

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level
then means at that moment in time

explanation.surface: A flag is raised over a temple at a given moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standard' reads as a flag, but means a norm or average, as in 'on a par'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Parthenon is the ancient temple of Athena on the Acropolis in Athens.

clue.text: Part of central US, typically lively

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A remark that part of the American heartland is usually full of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Lusty means vigorous and full of energy, a near synonym for spirited.
